investigationEvent.text: TC-M05: Patient T.P. (male, 55 years) was treated with Testdrugimab 200mg daily (combination product with Testdevice Auto-Injector) for rheumatoid arthritis starting 2026-01-15. The auto-injector device malfunctioned (problem code 4001) on first use. On 2026-03-01, nausea developed (resolved by 2026-03-10). On 2026-03-05, hepatic enzyme elevation was noted; ALT 850 U/L (normal 7-40), AST 760 U/L (normal 10-40). Drug was withdrawn. Patient developed progressive hepatic failure and died on 2026-03-12. Autopsy was performed; cause of death confirmed as hepatic failure. Medical history: hypertension (ongoing). Past drug: Ibuprofen 2020-2023 for RA. Concomitant: Lisinopril and Methotrexate. Sender diagnosis: Hepatic failure. Drug indication: Rheumatoid arthritis.

observationEvent.value: The onset of hepatic failure was rapid and unexpected given the patient's initial tolerance of Testdrugimab. The device malfunction on first use may have resulted in variable drug delivery. The causality assessment strongly implicates Testdrugimab as the primary cause of drug-induced liver injury progressing to hepatic failure. Autopsy findings confirmed hepatic necrosis consistent with drug-induced etiology.

observationEvent.value: A 55-year-old male with hypertension was initiated on Testdrugimab 200mg daily for rheumatoid arthritis. He had previously taken ibuprofen (2020-2023) which caused gastritis. On day 45 of treatment he developed nausea (resolved day 54) and markedly elevated liver enzymes (ALT 850 U/L, AST 760 U/L; bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL). Drug was discontinued. Despite cessation, the patient progressed to hepatic failure and died on 2026-03-12. Reporter concludes Testdrugimab was the likely cause of drug-induced hepatic failure.
